To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

T-cell help is not restricted to B cells stimulated with antigen in the form of a hapten-carrier conjugate, but can also be delivered to B cells stimulated by a hapten-protein conjugate, provided that the antigen is presented in a soluble form and the homologous hapten-carrier is added to the culture.

the anamnesteric immune response of spleen cells to DNP- KLH is due to the combined action of two factors, one of which is a soluble T-helper factor, presumably identical to T-cell replacing factor, and that both factors are produced by the primed T-helper cell.
T-cell- replacing factors are generated by primed helper T cells upon rechallenge with antigen and help primed B cells in the anamnetic immune response to soluble antigens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of T-cell help to primed B cells in an anamnestic antibody response.
an in situ generation and function of a nonantigenspecific T-helper factor during the anannestic immune response in vitro.
the mechanism of T-cell help to B cells in the anamnetic immune response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the secondary immune response to soluble antigens, T-cell help can be mediated in a nonantigen specific manner by T-cell- replacing factors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

T-cell help in vitro is mediated by a T-helper factor that is generated in situ by T cells upon antigenic challenge and acts on primed B cells to promote their differentiation into IgG-secretering cells.

the anamnistic IgG response to a soluble protein antigen is the combined result of the direct action of carrier-specific helper T cells on B cells, as well as of the action of a T-cell-replacing factor, which is produced by carrier-specific helper T lymphocytes and which is capable of helping primed B lymphocytes to become IgG antibody-producing cells.

in vitro, T-cell- replacing activity can be induced in primed helper cells, which can help primed B cells to become IgG secreting cells, provided that the B cells are stimulated by soluble heteroclinic hapten carrier conjugates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the T-cell- replacing factors produced in the anamnetic response are not antigen-specific, but rather are directed against the carrier moiety.
